compiled_state.title: As a maintainer, all consumers of llm-api-call.sh and ci-llm-review-runner.sh are enumerated and migrated before deletion
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Enumerate every consumer of `llm-api-call.sh` and `ci-llm-review-runner.sh` across the entire repo and the `plugins/dso/` tree (scripts, skills, hooks, agent files, GitHub workflow YAML, docs, tests, fixtures), produce an exhaustive consumer list, update each consumer to invoke the new Python module path or the shim, and remove hardcoded path assumptions before S3 deletes / reduces those scripts.

**Why**: Red-team adversarial review surfaced this as a residual-references gap. S3 deletes `llm-api-call.sh` outright and reduces `ci-llm-review-runner.sh` to a shim. The Phase 1 Part C scan covered docs and tests but did not exhaustively enumerate hooks, skills, agent prompts, or workflow YAML — any of which may carry hardcoded references. Deleting / renaming a shared resource without a consumer enumeration pass causes broken references at runtime in arbitrary in-tree call sites.

**Scope**:
- IN: Exhaustive grep of repo + `plugins/dso/` tree (scripts, skills, hooks, agents, docs, workflow YAML, tests, fixtures) for `llm-api-call.sh` and `ci-llm-review-runner.sh` references; consumer list captured as an artifact; each consumer updated to invoke the new Python module path or the shim; hardcoded path assumptions removed.
- OUT: Removing the consumers themselves (only updating references); modifying the shim or Python module (those are S3); out-of-tree consumer outreach (deprecation note in S6).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, an exhaustive consumer list for both `llm-api-call.sh` and `ci-llm-review-runner.sh` has been produced and checked in (or attached as a story artifact). The list covers scripts, skills, hooks, agent files, GitHub workflow YAML, docs, tests, and fixtures.
  ← Satisfies: "References in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, ci-overlay-flags.md, and onboarding/SKILL.md updated" (extended scope per residual-references finding)
- When this story is complete, every in-tree reference to `llm-api-call.sh` invokes the new Python module path (or has been updated to a shim invocation), and every in-tree reference to `ci-llm-review-runner.sh` is explicitly aware of the shim semantics shipped in S3 (i.e., the contract S3 documents). Hardcoded path assumptions have been replaced with `_PLUGIN_ROOT`-relative or shim-mediated invocations.
  ← Satisfies: deletion-safety precondition for S3
- When this story is complete, a verification grep produces zero in-tree references to `llm-api-call.sh` after deletion and a documented set of references to `ci-llm-review-runner.sh` that exercise only the shim's stable invocation surface.
  ← Satisfies: SC1 deletion safety

## Considerations

- [Maintainability] The Phase 1 Part C scan covered docs and tests. This story extends that coverage to hooks, skills, agents, workflow YAML, and fixtures — anywhere a shell script can be referenced.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
